The table migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts` adds no unique index/constraint on `host`, and the model only has `validates_format_of :host` (no `validates_uniqueness_of`). Lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record to choose `category` (`eh.try(:category_id)`), so duplicates can cause nondeterministic selection of which category/record is used. | The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` without any uniqueness validation

records.issue_text: After save() succeeds, Discourse.Category.findById returns undefined when categoryId is null, so the UI displays a blank category (disagreeing with the persisted uncategorized default) until reload
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the component explicitly unwraps the buffer (`const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host')`) and after `host.save(props)` it manually mutates the model with `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`, rather than relying on the save response to hydrate relationships. Given the server serializer for `EmbeddableHost` only returns `:id, :host, :category_id` (no embedded `category` object), this manual step is an intentional workaround but is a substantive architecture/data-consistency
